Cc: legal@acme.com, procurement@acme.com

Subject: Product use / training rights question — Order Form draft attached

Hannah / Ben —

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our in-house counsel flagged two items we need to confirm before we can route to procurement:

1) Output ownership: Can you confirm Acme will retain exclusive ownership of outputs generated from our confidential prompts/data? We want a simple line in the order form that makes that explicit.

2) Model training / feedback license: We are ok with Redwood collecting telemetry for quality and product improvement, but Acme does NOT want Redwood to train models on Acme customer content or customer prompts unless we explicitly opt in and we receive compensation/credits. Would Redwood accept a narrow feedback license limited to aggregated and de-identified telemetry, excluding customer content and PII?

I've attached our redlined order form (ACME_OrderForm_v1_redlines.docx). Procurement asked for a short summary and proposed MSA language they can share with legal. Can you circle back with suggested language and expected time to finalize?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Product Partnerships | Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Product use / training rights question — Order Form draft attached

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the redline. High level: we can and want to accommodate Acme's preference to retain outputs and to avoid training on customer-controlled content unless there's an opt-in.

Proposed approach (short):
- Order Form: "Customer retains all rights, title and interest in Outputs generated by the Service from Customer Content."
- Feedback license: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use aggregated, de-identified operational telemetry and product usage data for the purpose of improving and operating the Service. 'Aggregated, de-identified' excludes raw customer content, prompts, and any data that could be re-identified as belonging to Customer or Customer's end users."
- Training carveout: "Redwood will not use Customer Content, Outputs, or end-user prompts to train or continually update models used to serve the Customer without Customer's prior written consent and a mutually agreed commercial arrangement."

If helpful, Laura can propose MSA-ready wording for the snippet to drop into the order form. Ben — do you want me to offer Acme a limited credit or service-level concession if they agree to a broader opt-in later?

Happy to hop on a quick call with Elena and Acme legal tomorrow to close.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
(hannah_schmitt@redwood.com)

Subject: Proposed MSA/order form language for Acme — draft attached

Hannah / Elena / Ben —

Based on the ask, I drafted the following MSA clause to slot into the Order Form or MSA. Please review and confirm. I'm attaching a plain-text snippet as well (proposed-msa-snippet.txt).

--- begin clause ---
Customer Outputs and Feedback. Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in Outputs produced by the Service from Customer Content.

Feedback and Service Data. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use aggregated, de-identified operational telemetry and usage metrics ("Service Data") to operate, improve, and develop the Service, provided that such Service Data does not include Customer Content, individual end-user prompts, or other information that could be re-identified to Customer or its end users.

Training Restriction. Redwood will not use Customer Content, Outputs, or end-user prompts to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update models used to serve Customer without Customer's prior written consent and a separately negotiated commercial agreement.

Security/Telemetry Exception. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use limited diagnostic logs or telemetry that contain transient, redacted identifiers solely for security monitoring, abuse detection, and incident response, provided Redwood follows data minimization and retention controls disclosed in the Data Processing Addendum.
--- end clause ---

Open questions for Acme legal:
- Is the "aggregated, de-identified" standard workable as written, or would you prefer enumerated technical controls (hashing, K-anonymity threshold, no raw log retention)?
- Is the Security/Telemetry Exception acceptable if we include a 30-day retention cap and access controls?

If we get a yes/no on those two points I can produce a redline-ready patch to the order form.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed-msa-snippet.txt (text/plain)

Subject: Re: Proposed MSA/order form language for Acme — draft attached

Thanks, Laura — that language looks good and addresses our concerns. A few points from Acme counsel:

- We prefer a short, enumerated set of technical controls for "de-identified" (removal of prompts, PII scrubbing, and no retention of raw prompts beyond 14 days) but the concept is acceptable.
- The Security/Telemetry Exception is acceptable if the 30-day retention cap is in place and Redwood documents access controls and audit logging.

Procurement will circulate to Acme legal for a final read; if all goes well they will request an updated Order Form with the clause and a DocuSign window next week. Can Redwood produce a redlined Order Form (with the clause inserted) and a one-page summary of what telemetry we would collect and how it is de-identified?

Elena Rossi
